title: Pure functions and side effects
learningObjectives: Explain pure functions and side effects and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: A pure function returns the same output for the same inputs and does not cause observable side effects. Side effects include changing external state, modifying arguments, writing to the DOM, logging, or making network requests. Many useful application functions are intentionally impure, but separating calculation from effects improves testing.
understand.whyItMatters: Pure functions are easier to test, reuse, and reason about. Keeping side effects at clear boundaries reduces hidden dependencies and accidental state changes.
understand.analogy: A pure function is like a calculator: the same inputs produce the same answer without changing the outside world.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: The function depends only on its parameters and returns a result without modifying external state.

examples.explanation: The function depends only on its parameters and returns a result without modifying external state.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a pure total-calculation function. Then write a separate function that updates the DOM using the returned result.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Pure functions and side effects</title></head><body>
<script>function calculateDiscount(price,rate){return price*(1-rate);}const result=calculateDiscount(100,.1);console.log(result);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which characteristic describes a pure function?
options: Same inputs produce the same output without observable side effects
questions.answer: Same inputs produce the same output without observable side effects
questions.explanation: A pure function is deterministic for its inputs and does not cause observable side effects.

questions.prompt: What makes a function easier to reason about?
options: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
